title: Priv EKS provisioner: declarative seed + sanity-harness for idempotent control-plane boot
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: private control plane provisioning for Redwood Private customers must be reliably idempotent, observable, and safe during upgrades. Current provisioner can leave partial control-plane state when a transient failure occurs (e.g., cross-account KMS timeout during initial bootstrap) which requires manual remediation. Proposal: build a lightweight "sanity-harness" and declarative seed mechanism that verifies a deterministic fingerprint of control-plane intent before and after provisioning, combined with a Merkle-style state signature stored alongside the Terraform state to enable safe retries and automatic reconcile decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Declarative seed flow implemented as a reusable Terraform module with documented inputs/outputs
Provisioner produces a deterministic provisioning fingerprint (resource list + critical attrs) and stores a signed Merkle manifest in customer S3 bucket
Sanity-harness validates fingerprint post-provision and returns machine-readable status via health webhook for the private control-plane operator
Edge case: if fingerprint mismatch is detected after partial runs, system surfaces a safe rollback plan and a dry-run terraform plan artifact for SRE debugging
Automated integration test that performs three failure-injection scenarios and demonstrates idempotent reconciliation without human rollback
updates: 2025-01-10 - Scoping: drafted PRD and prototype architecture for manifest signing using AWS KMS (customer-managed CMKs). Decided to use S3 object metadata + versioning to store Merkle manifests to avoid Dynamo table ops.

2025-01-16 - Spike complete: PoC generates stable resource fingerprints by normalizing provider IDs, sorting resources, and hashing critical attrs. Verified deterministic behavior across Terraform runs with same inputs (no drift).

2025-01-22 - Design decision: use a two-stage flow: (1) terraform-plan -> seed manifest generation (off-Terraform small Go utility) and (2) terraform-apply referencing the manifest. This minimizes Terraform lifecycle hacks and keeps module composable.

2025-01-30 - Implementation: initial module skeleton pushed (WIP). Created feature branch: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/priv-eks-seed/tree/feature/ENG-621409. Module includes hooks to upload manifest to S3 and a small health webhook lambda to report sanity results.

2025-02-03 - Integration tests added to CI job 'priv-provisioner/seed-sanity-integration'. First flaky failure found: IAM eventual consistency when creating cross-account roles. Added retry backoff in bootstrapper.
2025-02-05 - Security review requested. Need to confirm CMK key policies for signing manifests are compatible with both hosted KMS and customer-managed keys in tenant accounts.
comments: Liam O'Connor (2025-01-18): Suggest adding a short-lived 'seed session' token so we can tie apply runs to a manifest and reject accidental reuses from different commits.
Marta Reyes (2025-01-20): Agree on seed session token. Also propose a 'dry-run-only' mode that creates manifests and runs a validator without mutating infra for customer validation calls.
Priya Nair (Security) (2025-02-04): Question about signing: prefer envelope encryption with KMS Encrypt + signature stored separately to limit KMS Sign usage. We'll follow up with a short meeting.

Sven Johansson (Platform Infra) (2025-02-05): Noted cross-account assumption; add explicit docs and an optional module param to pre-create the S3 bucket and relevant policies when we control the account.
links: Incident reference: https://go.redwood.ai/incidents/2024-11-priv-provisioner-failure (for context on manual remediations)

notes: Follow-up tasks: (1) Finalize KMS signing approach (envelope vs sign), (2) Add canary scenario for upgrade path where manifest evolves (compare old vs new Merkle roots), (3) Add an operator API endpoint to 'accept' manifest after manual review for high-sensitivity customers. Also coordinate with Console team for a UI that surfaces manifest fingerprints and dry-run artifacts.
next_steps: Complete security review, stabilize cross-account IAM retries, merge initial module PR, run 3 clean integration runs against staging and record artifacts for runbook creation. Assign SRE for playbook and postmortem drills.
